How point buy works in 5e

Every score starts at 8 and you have 27 points to raise them. Each step up to 13 costs 1 point; 14 and 15 cost 2 each, so a 15 costs 9 points in all. You can't buy a score above 15 or leave one below 8. Racial bonuses come after, which is how a starting character reaches 16 or 17. The calculator greys out the + button when the next step costs more than you have left.

The four ways to set scores

  • Point buy: every character is equal, and you choose exactly where the strengths go. A common split is 15, 15, 15, 8, 8, 8 for a focused character, or 13, 13, 13, 12, 12, 12 for an all-rounder.
  • Standard array: 15, 14, 13, 12, 10, and 8, placed where you like. It's worth exactly 27 points, the same as point buy.
  • Roll 4d6, drop the lowest: roll four six-sided dice six times and add the highest three each time. The rolls go in the site's dice history, and the summary tells you what the set is worth in point buy, so the table can see whether it came out ahead.
  • Your own numbers: for a DM's house rule or scores rolled at the table.

Racial bonuses

RaceBonus
Hill dwarf+2 CON, +1 WIS
High elf+2 DEX, +1 INT
Lightfoot halfling+2 DEX, +1 CHA
Human+1 to every score
Dragonborn+2 STR, +1 CHA
Rock gnome+2 INT, +1 CON
Half-elf+2 CHA, +1 to two others
Half-orc+2 STR, +1 CON
Tiefling+2 CHA, +1 INT

A score's modifier is its value minus 10, halved and rounded down: 8 and 9 give −1, 10 and 11 give +0, up to +3 at 16 and 17. An odd score gives the same modifier as the even one below it, so it only pays off when something later adds 1: a 17 is a good start if you plan to raise it at level 4, and a 16 is just as strong until then.

Works with

⚖️ Arrange for Class puts the highest scores in the class's key abilities (Strength for a fighter, Wisdom for a cleric), then Constitution and Dexterity. 🧝 Send to Character Builder starts a new character in the Character Builder with these scores, race, and class, ready for its background, skills, gear, and spells. The Dice Roller keeps every 4d6 roll in its history.
